title: Isolating bias points, DC versus AC coupling

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Every transistor stage needs its own DC operating point, but stages must also pass signals to each other. Connecting them directly, **DC coupling**, makes the bias points depend on each other: whatever DC level one stage's output sits at is forced onto the next stage's input. Any drift in an early stage then propagates and is amplified like a signal.

**AC coupling** puts a capacitor in the signal path. It is an open circuit at DC, so each stage's bias network sets its own levels, and nearly a short at signal frequencies, so the signal passes. The same idea gives the **bypass capacitor**: a capacitor across a bias resistor keeps the resistor in the DC circuit but shorts it for signals. AC coupling is natural for discrete audio and RF stages. Integrated circuits avoid it, because large capacitors cost area and many signals contain DC; instead they use DC coupling with careful level planning, differential stages and feedback.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ Z_C = \frac1{j\omega C}: \quad |Z_C| \to \infty \ (\omega = 0), \quad |Z_C| \to 0 \ (\omega\ \text{large}) \]
\[ V_G = V_{DD}\frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2} \quad (\text{divider bias behind a coupling capacitor}) \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A gate needs 1.2 V from a 3.3 V supply. A divider with \(R_2 = 240\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) to ground and \(R_1 = 420\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) to the supply gives \(3.3\cdot240/660 = 1.2\ \mathrm{V}\). A microphone with any DC level can then be connected through a capacitor without disturbing that 1.2 V. With DC coupling instead, the previous stage's output would have to sit at exactly 1.2 V.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Including a source's DC offset in the bias calculation when it is behind a coupling capacitor.
- Forgetting that DC coupling ties the bias of one stage to the previous one.
- Assuming AC coupling is free: it blocks DC and needs large capacitors.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: A coupling capacitor and the resistance it feeds form a high-pass corner, the subject of low-frequency response. DC-coupled designs lean on differential pairs and on careful level planning in cascades.
